quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: When a national retail chain analyzed two years of exit survey data from departing employees across nearly a thousand store locations, it found that employees at stores with department managers who held brief one-on-one conversations at least once a month cited 'feeling undervalued' as a reason for leaving far less often than employees at stores where managers rarely held individual conversations, even though pay scales and job duties were standardized identically company-wide.
options: Regular one-on-one check-ins from managers seem to reduce employees' sense of being undervalued, apart from pay or duties.
Pay and job duties were the main factors in employees feeling undervalued.
Employees at stores with frequent check-ins cited feeling undervalued more often.
The frequency of manager conversations had no bearing on why employees left.
quests.correctAnswer: Regular one-on-one check-ins from managers seem to reduce employees' sense of being undervalued, apart from pay or duties.
quests.hint: Notice what stayed the same between the two groups of stores, and what differed.
quests.explanation: Feeling undervalued was cited less often at stores where managers held regular one-on-one conversations, even though pay and duties were identical everywhere, suggesting the personal check-ins themselves addressed something standardized policies alone could not.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Ecologists comparing two adjacent sections of a grassland reserve found that the section where controlled, low-intensity burns were conducted every three years supported a wider variety of native wildflower species than the section left entirely unburned, though both sections received identical rainfall and were grazed by the same number of animals throughout the entirety of the fifteen-year study, according to the research team's final published report.
options: Unburned grassland supported a greater variety of wildflower species.
Rainfall differences explain the difference in wildflower diversity between the sections.
Periodic controlled burns are associated with greater wildflower diversity than leaving grassland unburned.
Both sections supported an identical variety of wildflower species.
quests.correctAnswer: Periodic controlled burns are associated with greater wildflower diversity than leaving grassland unburned.
quests.hint: Compare wildflower diversity between the two sections, noting which factors were held equal.
quests.explanation: The regularly burned section supported more wildflower species than the unburned one, even with identical rainfall and grazing, suggesting the burning itself, not other environmental factors, was linked to the greater diversity.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A study following blended families for five years after remarriage found that stepparents who waited for the biological parent to establish most household rules and discipline during the first year, gradually taking on more of that role only as the stepchildren grew more comfortable, reported stronger relationships with their stepchildren by year five than stepparents who took an equal disciplinary role from the very beginning of the new household, according to the study's final interviews.
options: A gradual approach to discipline appears linked to stronger long-term stepparent-stepchild relationships.
Taking an equal disciplinary role immediately led to stronger relationships.
The timing of a stepparent's disciplinary role had no bearing on relationship quality.
Every family in the study reported identical relationship outcomes by year five.
quests.correctAnswer: A gradual approach to discipline appears linked to stronger long-term stepparent-stepchild relationships.
quests.hint: Compare relationship outcomes between stepparents who eased into discipline gradually and those who didn't.
quests.explanation: Stepparents who gradually took on a disciplinary role reported stronger relationships by year five than those who took an equal role immediately, suggesting a slower approach may help stepchildren adjust more comfortably.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team studying how people use fitness tracking wearables found that users who could see their heart rate data in real time during exercise adjusted their pace far more frequently mid-workout than users wearing a tracker that only displayed a summary after the workout ended, though total calories burned per session ended up nearly identical between both groups, based on data the team collected from several thousand recorded sessions.
options: Users with real-time data burned significantly more calories overall.
Access to real-time data had no bearing on how users adjusted their pace.
Users without real-time data adjusted their pace more frequently.
Real-time heart rate data changes how people adjust their effort, even without changing the overall workout result.
quests.correctAnswer: Real-time heart rate data changes how people adjust their effort, even without changing the overall workout result.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates what changed (pace adjustments) from what stayed the same (calories burned).
quests.explanation: Users with real-time heart rate data adjusted their pace more often mid-workout, yet total calories burned ended up similar either way, suggesting the data changed how people exercised in the moment without changing the ultimate outcome.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional airline that had always assigned seats randomly during check-in switched to a system letting passengers pay a small fee to select a specific seat in advance. Complaints about seating fell overall, but complaints specifically about being seated next to a stranger while traveling with a companion rose slightly among passengers who declined to pay the fee, since randomly assigned seats now clustered available pairs less predictably than before.
options: Every type of seating complaint decreased after the new system began.
Complaints about seating increased overall after the new system began.
The paid seat-selection system reduced complaints overall but created a new issue for passengers who didn't pay.
The new system had no effect on complaints from any passenger group.
quests.correctAnswer: The paid seat-selection system reduced complaints overall but created a new issue for passengers who didn't pay.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes an overall improvement alongside one specific group that experienced a new problem.
quests.explanation: Overall seating complaints dropped, but complaints about being separated from a companion rose among passengers who skipped the fee, suggesting the new system solved one problem while creating a smaller new one for a specific group.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A university writing center that tracked which students returned for a second tutoring appointment found that students paired with the same tutor for both sessions returned for a third appointment at higher rates than students who saw a different tutor each time, even though satisfaction ratings for individual sessions were rated similarly high by students regardless of whether the tutor changed between visits, according to the center's own tracking records.
options: Seeing a different tutor each time led to higher return rates.
Individual session satisfaction was rated much lower when the tutor changed.
Continuity with the same tutor seems to encourage students to keep returning, even though it doesn't change satisfaction with any single session.
Tutor continuity had no bearing on whether students returned for more sessions.
quests.correctAnswer: Continuity with the same tutor seems to encourage students to keep returning, even though it doesn't change satisfaction with any single session.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates what changed (return rates) from what stayed the same (session satisfaction).
quests.explanation: Students paired with the same tutor returned for more sessions, even though single-session satisfaction was similar either way, suggesting continuity built something beyond a single good session, such as trust or familiarity, that encouraged students to keep coming back.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team studying chronic pain management compared patients who kept a daily written log of their pain levels, activities, and mood to patients who received the same treatment plan without keeping any log. Patients who journaled reported feeling more in control of their condition in follow-up interviews conducted six months later, though their actual reported pain intensity scores on a standard medical scale were statistically similar to the non-journaling group's scores.
options: Journaling significantly reduced patients' actual pain intensity scores.
Journaling appears to improve patients' sense of control over their pain without necessarily reducing the pain itself.
Patients who journaled reported feeling less in control of their condition.
Keeping a pain log had no measurable effect on any aspect of patients' experience.
quests.correctAnswer: Journaling appears to improve patients' sense of control over their pain without necessarily reducing the pain itself.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates how patients felt about their condition from their actual measured pain scores.
quests.explanation: Patients who journaled felt more in control of their condition, even though their measured pain intensity was similar to patients who didn't journal, suggesting the practice changed patients' psychological relationship to their pain rather than the pain itself.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An analysis of long-term investors found that those who checked their retirement account balance only once per quarter reported lower investment-related anxiety and were less likely to make changes to their investment allocation during market downturns than investors who checked their balance daily, even though both groups held portfolios with similar overall risk levels, based on a survey of several thousand account holders conducted by an independent research firm.
options: Checking investments less frequently seems linked to lower anxiety and fewer impulsive changes during downturns.
Checking balances daily was linked to lower investment-related anxiety.
The frequency of checking balances had no bearing on investor behavior.
Portfolio risk levels differed significantly between the two groups of investors.
quests.correctAnswer: Checking investments less frequently seems linked to lower anxiety and fewer impulsive changes during downturns.
quests.hint: Compare the two groups' anxiety levels and behavior during downturns, noting that their portfolios were similar.
quests.explanation: Investors who checked their balances less often reported less anxiety and made fewer impulsive changes during downturns than daily checkers, even with similar portfolios, suggesting the frequency of checking itself, not the underlying risk, influenced investor behavior.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city that had always held its annual budget hearings on weekday afternoons, when few working residents could attend, moved the hearings to a single weekday evening session and added a live-streamed option for residents unable to attend in person. Attendance and public comments both increased substantially, with roughly a third of the comments that year coming from residents who watched the live stream rather than attending physically.
options: Adding an evening time slot and streaming option appears to have broadened public participation in the hearings.
Public participation declined after the hearing schedule and format changed.
The live-streamed option was used by almost no residents.
Only the timing of the hearing affected attendance, with the streaming option making no difference.
quests.correctAnswer: Adding an evening time slot and streaming option appears to have broadened public participation in the hearings.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates the effect of the new schedule from the effect of the streaming option.
quests.explanation: Attendance and comments both rose after the hearing moved to evenings and added streaming, with a meaningful share of comments coming through the stream specifically, suggesting both changes worked together to broaden participation.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional supermarket chain that redesigned its produce section to place misshapen or unusually sized fruits and vegetables in a clearly labeled 'ugly produce' bin at a discounted price found that overall produce waste at participating stores dropped by nearly a fifth, while sales of standard, uniformly shaped produce at full price remained essentially unchanged, based on inventory records the chain reviewed across dozens of participating locations over six months.
options: Sales of full-price produce dropped sharply after the bin was introduced.
Produce waste increased after the discounted bin was introduced.
The discounted bin had no measurable effect on overall produce waste.
The discounted bin appears to have reduced waste without pulling sales away from full-price produce.
quests.correctAnswer: The discounted bin appears to have reduced waste without pulling sales away from full-price produce.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates what changed (waste) from what stayed the same (full-price sales).
quests.explanation: Produce waste dropped after the discount bin was introduced, while full-price sales stayed steady, suggesting the bin found a use for produce that would have otherwise been thrown away, without simply shifting existing full-price customers toward the discount.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Researchers comparing residential lawns found that lawns converted from traditional turf grass to a mix of native, drought-tolerant plants required significantly less supplemental watering during a regional dry spell than neighboring turf lawns, and homeowners with converted lawns also reported spending markedly less time on weekly maintenance throughout the growing season, despite initial concerns voiced by several homeowners that native plantings would require more specialized, time-consuming care.
options: Native plant lawns appear to require less water and less maintenance than traditional turf, contrary to some homeowners' expectations.
Native plant lawns required more water than traditional turf lawns.
Homeowners with native plantings spent more time on weekly maintenance.
Water and maintenance needs were identical between the two types of lawns.
quests.correctAnswer: Native plant lawns appear to require less water and less maintenance than traditional turf, contrary to some homeowners' expectations.
quests.hint: Notice what homeowners expected before converting their lawns, and compare it with what the passage says actually happened.
quests.explanation: Converted lawns needed less water and less maintenance time than traditional turf, despite some homeowners initially expecting the opposite, suggesting native plantings were more practical than commonly assumed, at least under dry conditions.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A youth soccer club that introduced a policy requiring coaches to rotate which players started each game, rather than always starting the same top performers, tracked player retention over three seasons and found that while retention among the club's most skilled players dropped slightly, overall club-wide retention rose because far fewer players of moderate ability quit partway through the season, according to registration records compiled at the end of each season studied.
options: Retention improved among every category of player after the policy began.
The rotation policy appears to have benefited overall retention even though it slightly reduced retention of top players.
Retention declined overall after the rotation policy was introduced.
The rotation policy had no measurable effect on player retention of any kind.
quests.correctAnswer: The rotation policy appears to have benefited overall retention even though it slightly reduced retention of top players.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes two different trends among two different groups of players.
quests.explanation: Top players' retention dropped slightly, but overall retention rose because fewer moderate-ability players quit, suggesting the rotation policy traded a small loss among elite players for a larger gain in keeping the broader player base engaged.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional theater festival that had always required playwrights to submit full scripts for consideration switched to accepting ten-minute staged readings of unfinished work in progress. Festival organizers reported that the plays ultimately selected for full production under the new system received stronger reviews on average than plays selected under the old full-script system, though organizers also noted the new process required significantly more staff time to administer each season.
options: The new process improved selection quality with no added administrative cost.
Plays selected under the new system received weaker reviews on average.
The staged-reading process appears to have improved selection quality at the cost of greater administrative effort.
The submission format had no bearing on the quality of selected plays.
quests.correctAnswer: The staged-reading process appears to have improved selection quality at the cost of greater administrative effort.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions both a benefit and a cost of the new selection process.
quests.explanation: Plays selected through staged readings received stronger reviews than those selected the old way, though the new process took more staff time, suggesting the improved quality came with a real trade-off in administrative effort.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team analyzing support tickets for a project management tool found that customers whose first support interaction was resolved by the same representative from start to finish, without being transferred between departments, gave dramatically higher satisfaction ratings than customers who were transferred at least once, even when the total time to resolution was measured to be similar between both groups, according to a review of several thousand tickets closed that quarter.
options: Avoiding transfers between representatives seems to matter more to customer satisfaction than how quickly an issue gets resolved.
Being transferred between departments led to higher satisfaction ratings.
Resolution time was the only factor that affected customer satisfaction.
Satisfaction ratings were identical regardless of whether customers were transferred.
quests.correctAnswer: Avoiding transfers between representatives seems to matter more to customer satisfaction than how quickly an issue gets resolved.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates satisfaction ratings from resolution time, which stayed similar between groups.
quests.explanation: Customers who dealt with a single representative rated their experience much higher than transferred customers, even with similar resolution times, suggesting the continuity of dealing with one person mattered more to satisfaction than speed alone.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A professional services firm that had always required partners to personally approve every client invoice before it was sent, regardless of amount, raised that threshold so that only invoices above a certain amount needed partner approval, with smaller invoices approved automatically by the billing system. Average time between completing work and sending an invoice dropped substantially, and no measurable increase in billing errors was reported over the following year.
options: Billing errors increased noticeably after the approval threshold was raised.
The time between completing work and sending invoices increased under the new policy.
The change in approval process had no measurable effect on billing speed.
Automating approval for smaller invoices appears to have sped up billing without increasing errors.
quests.correctAnswer: Automating approval for smaller invoices appears to have sped up billing without increasing errors.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions two separate outcomes: billing speed and error rates.
quests.explanation: Invoices went out faster after smaller ones no longer required partner approval, and billing errors didn't measurably increase, suggesting the automation streamlined the process without introducing new mistakes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A pediatric sleep specialist who counsels parents of toddlers found that families who maintained an identical bedtime routine, in the same order every single night, reported that their toddlers fell asleep faster on average than families whose bedtime routines varied somewhat from night to night, even though both groups reported starting the bedtime process at roughly the same time each evening, based on sleep diaries families kept for the specialist's ongoing research.
options: Starting bedtime at the same time each night was the only factor that mattered.
Families with varied routines reported faster sleep onset.
The order of a bedtime routine had no bearing on how quickly toddlers fell asleep.
Consistency in the order of a bedtime routine seems to matter more than simply starting at the same time each night.
quests.correctAnswer: Consistency in the order of a bedtime routine seems to matter more than simply starting at the same time each night.
quests.hint: Notice what stayed the same between the two groups (start time) and what differed (routine consistency).
quests.explanation: Toddlers fell asleep faster in families with an identical nightly routine order, even though both groups started at similar times, suggesting the predictability of the routine's sequence mattered more than the clock time alone.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A workplace wellness program that offered employees a financial incentive tied specifically to attending a certain number of gym sessions found that participation dropped sharply within a few months of the incentive being removed, falling to levels similar to employees who had never received any incentive at all during the entire two-year study, suggesting the original increase in gym attendance may not have reflected a lasting change in exercise habits.
options: Gym attendance remained high even after the incentive was removed.
Employees who never received an incentive attended the gym most consistently.
The incentive-driven attendance increase does not appear to have created a lasting exercise habit.
The incentive had a permanent effect on employees' exercise habits.
quests.correctAnswer: The incentive-driven attendance increase does not appear to have created a lasting exercise habit.
quests.hint: Notice what happened to attendance after the financial incentive was taken away.
quests.explanation: Attendance dropped back to baseline levels once the incentive was removed, suggesting the original increase was tied to the reward itself rather than reflecting a genuine, lasting change in employees' exercise habits.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: An online furniture retailer that added a feature allowing customers to see how a piece of furniture would look in a room using their phone's camera found that customers who used the feature before purchasing returned items at a lower rate than customers who did not use it, but also found that customers using the feature took, on average, several days longer to complete their purchase after first viewing a product online.
options: The visualization feature appears to reduce returns while also slowing down the purchase decision.
The feature reduced both returns and the time to complete a purchase.
Customers who used the feature returned items more often.
The feature had no measurable effect on returns or purchase timing.
quests.correctAnswer: The visualization feature appears to reduce returns while also slowing down the purchase decision.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes two separate effects of the feature moving in different directions.
quests.explanation: Customers using the visualization feature returned fewer items but took longer to decide, suggesting the feature helped them make more confident choices even though it extended the time before they committed to buying.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A district that piloted a program allowing high school students to retake a failed unit test after completing a short review packet, rather than simply receiving a permanent failing grade, found that students who retook tests under this system passed the overall course at higher rates, but teachers also reported spending considerably more time each week grading the additional retest attempts, according to a survey the district conducted of participating teachers at the end of the pilot year.
options: The retest policy improved pass rates without any added workload for teachers.
The retest policy appears to have improved pass rates at the cost of additional teacher workload.
Pass rates declined among students who used the retest policy.
Teacher workload was unaffected by the new retest policy.
quests.correctAnswer: The retest policy appears to have improved pass rates at the cost of additional teacher workload.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions both a benefit for students and a cost for teachers.
quests.explanation: Pass rates rose under the retest policy, but teachers reported a real increase in grading workload, suggesting the improvement for students came with a genuine added cost for staff.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A ski resort that had always included lift ticket costs bundled into all-inclusive vacation packages began offering an unbundled option where guests could purchase lodging separately from lift access. Bookings from experienced skiers, who often already owned season passes elsewhere, increased under the unbundled option, while bookings from beginner-focused travel groups, who valued the simplicity of one combined price, decreased slightly during that first full season, according to the resort's own booking data.
options: Unbundling prices appealed equally to both experienced and beginner skiers.
Bookings from beginner groups increased after the unbundled option was introduced.
Unbundling prices appears to have appealed to experienced skiers while making the resort slightly less attractive to beginners.
The pricing structure had no bearing on which types of travelers booked.
quests.correctAnswer: Unbundling prices appears to have appealed to experienced skiers while making the resort slightly less attractive to beginners.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes opposite trends for two different types of travelers.
quests.explanation: Experienced skiers booked more under the unbundled option while beginner groups booked slightly less, suggesting the change appealed to travelers who wanted flexibility but was less convenient for those who valued a simple combined price.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Researchers studying two colonies of the same bee species, one located near a large area of wildflower meadow and one located near a monoculture crop field with only a single blooming plant species, found that the colony near the diverse meadow produced significantly more honey and showed lower rates of colony collapse over a three-year period, despite both colonies receiving identical care and disease treatment from their respective beekeepers throughout the study.
options: The monoculture field colony produced more honey and showed better health.
Beekeeper care was the main factor explaining the difference between colonies.
Both colonies showed identical rates of honey production and colony collapse.
Access to diverse flowering plants appears linked to better bee colony health and honey production.
quests.correctAnswer: Access to diverse flowering plants appears linked to better bee colony health and honey production.
quests.hint: Compare the two colonies' outcomes, noting that beekeeper care was the same for both.
quests.explanation: The colony near diverse wildflowers produced more honey and collapsed less often than the colony near a single crop species, even with identical care, suggesting access to varied flowering plants itself supported better colony health.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city that had always required residents to call a general municipal phone line to report potholes, often waiting on hold or being transferred between departments, launched a mobile app allowing residents to photograph and pin the exact location of a pothole. Average repair time from report to fix dropped substantially, and the public works department noted that photographed reports required far less follow-up communication to confirm the exact problem and its precise location.
options: Repair times increased after the app was introduced.
The app appears to have sped up repairs by giving public works clearer information upfront.
The app required more follow-up communication than phone reports did.
The method of reporting potholes had no bearing on repair times.
quests.correctAnswer: The app appears to have sped up repairs by giving public works clearer information upfront.
quests.hint: Think about what information a photo and pinned location provide that a phone call might not.
quests.explanation: Repair times dropped and follow-up communication decreased after residents began using the app, suggesting that photos and precise locations gave public works clearer information than phone reports had, reducing time spent clarifying the problem.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A regional theater chain that tested reserved seating at several previously first-come, first-served locations found that reserved-seating theaters saw a slight decline in same-day ticket purchases but a substantial increase in tickets purchased more than three days in advance, resulting in overall attendance that was roughly the same as before the change, though total revenue increased slightly due to a small booking fee charged only on advance tickets.
options: Reserved seating significantly increased overall attendance.
Reserved seating appears to have shifted when tickets were purchased without changing overall attendance much.
Reserved seating significantly decreased overall attendance.
Reserved seating had no effect on when tickets were purchased.
quests.correctAnswer: Reserved seating appears to have shifted when tickets were purchased without changing overall attendance much.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes a shift in timing of purchases rather than a change in the total number sold.
quests.explanation: Same-day purchases dropped while advance purchases rose, leaving overall attendance about the same, suggesting reserved seating changed the timing of when people bought tickets more than it changed how many people ultimately attended.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A credit counseling nonprofit that offers free one-on-one budgeting sessions found that clients who brought a family member or partner to their sessions were more likely to still be following their budget plan one year later than clients who attended sessions alone, even though the actual budgeting advice given during the sessions did not differ in content based on whether a client attended alone or with someone else, according to the nonprofit's own follow-up surveys.
options: Clients who attended alone were more likely to follow their budget a year later.
Attending budgeting sessions with a family member or partner seems linked to sticking with the plan longer.
The advice given differed significantly depending on who attended the session.
Whether a client attended alone or with someone else had no bearing on long-term follow-through.
quests.correctAnswer: Attending budgeting sessions with a family member or partner seems linked to sticking with the plan longer.
quests.hint: Notice that the advice itself was the same either way; only the presence of a companion differed.
quests.explanation: Clients who brought someone to their budgeting session stuck with their plan longer, even though the advice given was identical either way, suggesting having a companion involved may provide ongoing support that helps the plan stick.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A collegiate track program that switched from a single annual time trial to determine race lineups to a rolling average of a runner's best three times over the season found that overall team times improved, and coaches reported that runners seemed less prone to disappointment after a single off day, since one poor performance no longer determined their standing for the rest of the season, according to coaches interviewed at the season's end.
options: The rolling average system worsened both team performance and runner morale.
A single time trial remained the most accurate predictor of runner ability.
The scoring method had no bearing on team performance or runner morale.
Using a rolling average appears to have improved both team performance and runners' resilience to a single bad day.
quests.correctAnswer: Using a rolling average appears to have improved both team performance and runners' resilience to a single bad day.
quests.hint: Notice the passage mentions two separate positive outcomes of the new scoring system.
quests.explanation: Team times improved and runners seemed less discouraged by single off days under the rolling-average system, suggesting the new method benefited both performance and how runners emotionally handled an occasional bad race.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A meal-delivery company that tested sending recipe instructions as a short video instead of a printed card found that customers following the video completed meals in less time on average, but customer surveys revealed no significant difference in how customers rated the taste or presentation of the finished dish compared to customers who used the traditional printed instructions, based on a survey sent to several thousand customers after delivery.
options: Video instructions led to noticeably better-tasting finished dishes.
Customers using video instructions took longer to complete their meals.
The format of the instructions had no bearing on preparation time.
Video instructions appear to save preparation time without changing how the finished dish turns out.
quests.correctAnswer: Video instructions appear to save preparation time without changing how the finished dish turns out.
quests.hint: Notice the passage separates preparation time from how the finished dish was rated.
quests.explanation: Customers using video instructions cooked faster, but the finished dish was rated similarly regardless of instruction format, suggesting the video helped with efficiency without actually changing the quality of the final result.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A team studying smart doorbell camera usage found that households that placed the camera at a lower height, roughly at eye level for an average adult, correctly identified more delivery packages and visitors in recorded footage than households with cameras mounted higher up near the roofline for a broader view of the property, even though the higher-mounted cameras technically covered a wider overall field of view, according to the team's video analysis.
options: Higher-mounted cameras identified more visitors and packages correctly.
Camera placement at eye level appears more useful for identification than a wider field of view from a higher mount.
Camera height had no bearing on how accurately footage identified visitors.
Field of view was the only factor that affected identification accuracy.
quests.correctAnswer: Camera placement at eye level appears more useful for identification than a wider field of view from a higher mount.
quests.hint: Notice that a wider field of view did not translate into better identification results.
quests.explanation: Eye-level cameras identified visitors and packages more accurately than higher-mounted ones, even though the higher cameras covered more area, suggesting a closer, more direct view mattered more for identification than overall coverage.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A city comparing two methods of encouraging residential composting, a bin drop-off subsidy versus free curbside pickup added to existing trash collection, found that curbside pickup resulted in dramatically higher participation, but a follow-up survey found that compost quality, meaning how well residents sorted out non-compostable contamination, was noticeably better among the smaller group of participants using the subsidized bin drop-off system, according to samples the city tested that year.
options: Curbside pickup resulted in both higher participation and better-sorted compost.
Curbside pickup drew more participants, while drop-off bins appeared to produce cleaner, better-sorted compost.
The bin drop-off subsidy resulted in lower participation and worse-sorted compost.
The method of composting had no bearing on either participation or compost quality.
quests.correctAnswer: Curbside pickup drew more participants, while drop-off bins appeared to produce cleaner, better-sorted compost.
quests.hint: Notice the passage describes two different methods each doing better on a different measure.
quests.explanation: Curbside pickup increased participation, but drop-off bins produced better-sorted compost, suggesting each method had a different strength rather than one method being simply superior to the other in every way.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: A manufacturing company that introduced a suggestion program, where any employee could submit ideas for improving factory processes and receive a small bonus for ideas that were implemented, found that the majority of implemented suggestions came from employees on the factory floor rather than from engineers or managers, a pattern that surprised leadership, who had expected most useful ideas to come from technical staff rather than from workers directly operating the machinery each day.
options: Employees directly operating the machinery appear to have generated more practical improvement ideas than leadership expected.
Most implemented suggestions came from engineers and managers, as leadership had expected.
The suggestion program produced no useful ideas from any group of employees.
Leadership correctly predicted which employees would contribute the most useful ideas.
quests.correctAnswer: Employees directly operating the machinery appear to have generated more practical improvement ideas than leadership expected.
quests.hint: Compare what leadership expected with what the passage says actually happened.
quests.explanation: Most implemented suggestions came from factory floor workers rather than technical staff, contrary to leadership's expectations, suggesting that employees closest to the daily work may notice practical improvements that those higher up the chain overlook.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct conclusion.
quests.passage: Since switching to a reusable produce bag set instead of using the thin plastic bags provided in the grocery store's produce section, the Nakamura family estimated they have used roughly six hundred fewer plastic bags over the past year, though they also noted that a couple of their more delicate reusable bags have already torn and needed replacing sooner than they originally expected when they first purchased the set.
options: The switch to reusable bags increased the family's overall plastic use.
The reusable bags have shown no signs of wear over the year.
Switching to reusable bags appears to have reduced plastic use, though not without some added cost from replacing worn bags.
The switch to reusable bags had no effect on the family's plastic consumption.
